name: ensemble_signal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, four algorithmically-watched signals — session VWAP deviation, EMA trend alignment (1-min vs 5-min), Bollinger Band position, and 2-min RSI — are monitored by distinct participant archetypes: VWAP-benchmarked institutional desks, short-term trend systems, volatility traders, and momentum-fade algos. When at least 3 of these 4 signals simultaneously agree on direction, it identifies the 'trend-pullback-oversold' microstructure state: NIFTY is in an established short-term uptrend (EMA12 > EMA60), has briefly dipped below session VWAP under selling pressure (VWAP deviation +1), and RSI has reached a short-term oversold level (<35), while Bollinger Bands remain neutral. This convergence signals that multiple algorithm types are about to layer buy orders simultaneously, creating a 10-20 spot point directional push over the next 30-90 seconds as the brief flush exhausts and TWAP/VWAP algorithms resume accumulating.

indicators.name: session_vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative(close * volume) / cumulative(volume) from session open each day
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP from 09:15 each day — no scaling needed as it is a running measure. A deviation of >0.1% (threshold tunable) on NIFTY (~24 spot pts) is large enough to engage VWAP-benchmarked institutional desks who then provide the counter-pressure that drives reversion.

indicators.name: ema_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute EMA — the short-term trend proxy. At 5s bars, 12 bars = 60s = 1 minute. This is the fast signal that responds to the current directional push within the last minute. Original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars (~9-min window); compressed to 1-min here because we hold 30-90s, not 15-60 min.

indicators.name: ema_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute EMA — the medium-term trend context filter. At 5s bars, 60 bars = 5 minutes. When EMA12 > EMA60, the 1-minute micro-trend is aligned with the 5-minute trend — institutional directional orders are active. Original used EMA(21) on 1-min bars (~21-min window); compressed to 5-min here to match our shorter hold time.

indicators.name: bollinger_60_2
indicators.purpose: 5-minute Bollinger Bands (2σ). Breakout above upper band = strong bullish momentum; below lower band = strong bearish. Originally 20 bars on 1-min = 20-min BB; compressed to 60 bars = 5-min BB because our hold time is 30-90s and a 5-min breakout is still statistically significant and actionable at this frequency. Importantly, this sub-signal OPPOSES RSI at extremes — capturing the useful tension that filters for genuine multi-archetype consensus.

indicators.name: rsi_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute RSI — detects short-term oversold/overbought. At 5s bars, 24 bars = 120s = 2 minutes. RSI below 35 indicates brief flush/capitulation in price; above 65 indicates brief euphoria. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min bars (~14-min lookback); compressed to 2-min because we need the indicator to reflect extremes in the sub-5-minute timeframe we are trading. Wilder smoothing used for stability.

indicators.name: ensemble_score
indicators.purpose: Sum of four sub-signals. Score ≥ 3 means ≥ 3 of 4 sub-strategies bullish. Score ≤ -3 means bearish consensus. The threshold (default 3) is the key tunable — it controls signal frequency vs. quality trade-off.

conditions: sub2_ema = +1 (EMA12 > EMA60, confirming 5-min uptrend as anchor)
Score persists for 2 consecutive 5s bars (10s confirmation to filter 5s noise spikes)
sub2_ema = -1 (EMA12 < EMA60, confirming 5-min downtrend as anchor)
Score persists for 2 consecutive 5s bars (10s confirmation)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. In a 30-90s window, if NIFTY moves more than 8 pts against a multi-indicator consensus signal, the underlying thesis (coordinated algorithmic accumulation) has failed — the competing algorithms have reversed or the expected continuation did not materialize. 4 pts is tight enough to limit damage but wide enough to avoid noise (typical 5s NIFTY fluctuations are 1-3 pts).
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. The 'trend-pullback-oversold' setup on NIFTY typically generates a 15-25 spot point continuation move in 30-90 seconds as TWAP algorithms resume. Targeting 14 pts captures ~60% of the expected move, giving a 1:1.75 R:R. Avoids being greedy on a setup that fundamentally requires the flush to be brief.

filters.vix_filter: none — ensemble score provides implicit regime filter
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; first 15 minutes excluded for EMA/RSI warmup
filters.volume_filter: none explicit — NIFTY index volume is structural
filters.trend_filter: EMA12 vs EMA60 alignment is embedded in Sub2
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close price

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-medium — all sub-signals are well-known, but the specific 3/4 consensus threshold on NIFTY at 5s is less crowded than any individual signal. The rarity of the setup (3-8 per day) limits capacity but maintains edge.

adaptation_notes: Original ran on NIFTY 50 stocks with stock-specific filters (ADV, earnings exclusion, bid-ask spread). All stock-specific filters dropped — NIFTY index has no earnings events, no ADV concern, and limit-order execution eliminates spread cost. Timeframe compressed from 1-min to 5-second bars, hold time from 15-60 min to 30-90 seconds. EMA windows scaled from 9/21-min to 1-min/5-min to match the shorter hold time. RSI scaled from 14-min to 2-min for the same reason. Bollinger scaled from 20-min to 5-min. VWAP unchanged as a cumulative session measure. The 2-bar persistence filter is new — replaces the 2-bar confirmation in the original but at 5s granularity (10s vs 2-min confirmation). The fundamental ensemble thesis — that coincident agreement across diverse signal archetypes identifies high-conviction directional states — translates directly and perhaps more cleanly to the NIFTY index where individual signals are less noisy than on individual stocks.
weaknesses: Sub-signals are structurally correlated on NIFTY: in trending markets, EMA and BB agree while VWAP and RSI oppose — genuine 3/4 consensus is rare (3-8 times/day), limiting daily P&L
2-minute RSI at 5s bars may produce false oversold/overbought readings during choppy intraday sessions — Sub4 is the weakest of the four sub-signals

The BB breakout signal (Sub3) at 5-min scale will rarely co-occur with VWAP below (Sub1=+1) because a BB breakout means price is well above the mean — this structural tension limits bullish consensus paths
At only 3-8 signals/day on a single index (NIFTY), variance is very high over a 12-day evaluation window
